- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, check for overshoot after spike — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward movement after a spike, model often fails to correct — adjust forecast downward by 3–5% of recent range if sentiment is low or neutral.
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85) and model continues upward, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00, model tends to be overly conservative — allow 1–2% upward bias if recent price is rising.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust forecast to align with early sentiment-driven volatility.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model may be underestimating risk — add 1–3% upward buffer if price is trending down.
